newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears aid to Aircraft Services Lemwerder.
newsitem.headline: EU clears aid to Aircraft Services Lemwerder.

text.p: The European Commission said it approved aid measures totalling 70 million German marks granted by the German state of Land Lower Saxony to Aircraft Services Lemwerder (ASL), but with conditions.
"The Commission considered that the aid complies with the Community guidelines on state aid for rescuing and restructuring of firms in difficulties," the Commission said in a statement.

"The Commission however considered that its authorisation must be made subject to the specific condition that the German authorities refrain until December 31 2001 from granting any ad hoc aid capable of contributing to an increase in the production capacity of ASL or of helping to cover any losses incurred by it," it added.
ASL, a former unit of DASA, specialises in the maintenance of civil aircraft.

The Commission said it had noted that there was a significant reduction in capacity, that the company had been privatised and that there was an important contribution by investors' own resources. These would also take over full entrepreneurial risk.
"All these elements allowed the Commission to conclude that the long-term viability of the company can be restored by the restructuring measures executed by ASL," it said.
